name: Electric Bicycle
description: A device with a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal assist to 20 mph, throttle to 20 mph, or pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts
Class 1: pedal assist only, ceasing at 20 mph; Class 2: propels it to 20 mph whether or not the rider pedals, cutting out when the brakes are applied; Class 3: pedal assist only, ceasing at 28 mph
Riders of a Class 3 must be 14 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Riders and passengers under 18 on a Class 3 must wear a properly fitted and fastened CPSC- or ASTM-compliant bicycle helmet
Since January 1, 2018, manufacturers must permanently affix a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
restrictions.citation: Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a, added by 2017 Public Act 139

restrictions.rule: Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match; modified beyond the class limits, or with a motor over 750 watts, it's no longer an electric bicycle
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Subject to the same rules as a bicycle and not a motor vehicle or moped: no driver's license, registration or insurance
Ridden on any part of a highway open to bicycles, including bike lanes and shoulders, and on sidewalks where bicycles are allowed
Barred from cities that ban nonemergency motor vehicles unless the city council allows it, and from Mackinac Island State Park without a permit from its commission
Class 1 may use paved, crushed-limestone and rail trails unless the agency that manages the trail bans it; Class 2 and Class 3 may use them only if that agency allows it
Barred from nonmotorized natural-surface trails unless the agency that manages the trail allows it
A local authority or state agency must hold a public hearing before it bans, allows or regulates e-bikes

On DNR land, Class 1 may use state park, recreation area and state forest trails open to bicycles (except state game and wildlife areas and some named pathways); Class 2 needs a free disability permit, and Class 3 is barred
